The maker (wallet user) invalidates a previously-signed limit order. Maps to Amm::CancelIntentOrder on the OneInchLimitOrder venue; order_hash = the bytes32 orderHash arg. verifying_contract = $to (the v6 router).

1inch LOP v4 maker batch cancellation: cancelOrders(uint256[] makerTraits, bytes32[] orderHashes) on AggregationRouterV6 0x111111125421ca6dc452d289314280a0f8842a65 (selector 0x89e7c650). array_emit over orderHashes (bytes32[], scalar element bound to bare $inputs) → one Amm::CancelIntentOrder per hash. The parallel makerTraits[] does not change cancel semantics, so it is not decoded. verifying_contract = $to (the v6 router).

Off-chain EIP-712 maker-sign of a 1inch Limit Order Protocol v4 Order. domain="1inch Aggregation Router" v6, verifying_contract=AggregationRouterV6 0x111111125421ca6dc452d289314280a0f8842a65 (LOP v4 is embedded in the v6 router), primary_type=Order. selector 0x00000001 is a sign-only placeholder (no on-chain call); routing is by (verifying_contract, primary_type) via the typed-data bridge. The EIP-712 Order declares maker/receiver/makerAsset/takerAsset as `address` (Solidity calldata packs them as uint256 Address) so the message fields resolve directly to addresses. valid_until via maker_traits_expiry $fn (MakerTraits bits 80..120 = uint40 unix-seconds; 0=never-expires remapped to max sentinel). recipient via coalesce_address $fn (Order.receiver==0 means the maker is the recipient).

On-chain commit of a 1inch native limit order. NativeOrderFactory.create((uint256x8)=IOrderMixin.Order) (selector 0x8c72b608, NativeOrderFactory 0xe12e0f117d23a5ccc57f8935cd8c4e80cd91ff01) — the on-chain twin of the off-chain order-sign@1.0.0 (same LOP v4 Order struct). The maker (msg.sender) opens an order selling makerAsset (always WETH for native orders; the clone wraps the user's ETH, msg.value==makingAmount) for takerAsset, deploying a per-order NativeOrderImpl CREATE2 clone. Calldata declares maker/receiver/makerAsset/takerAsset as AddressLib-packed uint256 (low 160 bits = address) so each resolves via address_from_uint256 (the typed-data sign path had address-typed fields and did NOT need it). recipient via coalesce_address(receiver, maker) (receiver!=0 enforced on-chain, but kept for parity). valid_until via maker_traits_expiry(makerTraits) (bits 80..120 uint40, 0=never -> max sentinel). Maps to Amm::SignIntentOrder on OneInchLimitOrder venue, order_kind=limit, OnchainTx nature. The clone's maker cancelOrder/withdraw live at non-fixed CREATE2 addresses (child universe) -> deferred, not in this manifest.

Aave V3.4+ Pool.approvePositionManager(positionManager,approve). Official Aave V3 Origin IPool states this grants the position manager permission to call setUserUseReserveAsCollateralOnBehalfOf and setUserEModeOnBehalfOf for the user, so this is a permission-delegation primitive and must be COVER.
Aave V3 Pool.deposit(asset,amount,onBehalfOf,referralCode) is the deprecated alias of supply with identical user-fund-move semantics.
Aave V3.4+ Pool inherits OpenZeppelin Multicall. Decode each bytes[] item recursively against the same Pool so bundled supply/withdraw/position-manager calls retain their concrete ActionBody shapes.

Aave V3.4+ Pool.renouncePositionManagerRole(user). The caller revokes its own position-manager permission for `user`; model as the same account-wide lending authorization primitive with authorizer=user, authorized=tx.from, is_authorized=false.

Aave V3 Pool.repayWithPermit — repay + bundled EIP-2612 permit (the permit grants the Pool ERC20 allowance in the same call). emit.body is the SAME RepayAction shape as aave/v3/repay@1.0.0: asset/amount/onBehalfOf carry the lending intent. The interestRateMode arg (Aave DataTypes.InterestRateMode: 1=STABLE, 2=VARIABLE) is mapped onto RepayAction.rate_mode via a $match value-map (1->stable, 2->variable) — exactly as repay@1.0.0. This is the mode of the debt being repaid, so it maps directly (no complement). The four trailing permit args (deadline/permitV/permitR/permitS) are bundled approval authorization, NOT part of the repay intent, so they are decoded but left UNREFERENCED in emit.body. The wallet's standalone EIP-2612 sign is handled by A.1's standard/erc20/permit route.
Aave V3.4+ Pool.setUserEModeOnBehalfOf(categoryId,onBehalfOf). This is the position-manager execution path for the same user-facing eMode toggle; `on_behalf_of` preserves the affected account.

Aave V3 Pool.setUserUseReserveAsCollateral(asset, useAsCollateral). The useAsCollateral bool selects between TWO distinct LendingAction variants — an action-tag-level switch, not a field value — so the `lending` sub-object is itself a $match value-map: true -> enable_collateral, false -> disable_collateral. Both branches carry the same SetCollateralAction shape (venue + asset) and share the emit.live_inputs (reserve_state + user_state_before). After value-map resolution the body is a normal nested-twice lending body that flatten_body decodes straight into LendingAction::EnableCollateral / DisableCollateral.

Aave V3.4+ Pool.setUserUseReserveAsCollateralOnBehalfOf(asset,useAsCollateral,onBehalfOf). This is the position-manager execution path for the same collateral toggle; `on_behalf_of` preserves the affected account.

Aave V3 Pool.supplyWithPermit — supply + bundled EIP-2612 permit (the permit grants the Pool ERC20 allowance in the same call). emit.body is the SAME SupplyAction shape as aave/v3/supply@1.0.0: only asset/amount/onBehalfOf carry the lending intent. The four trailing permit args (deadline/permitV/permitR/permitS) are bundled approval authorization, NOT part of the supply intent, so they are decoded by abi_fragment but left UNREFERENCED in emit.body. A future enrichment could emit Multicall[erc20_permit, supply]; for now the lending intent = SupplyAction, and the wallet's standalone EIP-2612 sign is handled by A.1's standard/erc20/permit route.

Aave V3 Pool.swapBorrowRateMode(asset, interestRateMode). Per the legacy Aave V3 IPool NatSpec the interestRateMode arg is 'The current interest rate mode of the position being swapped: 1 for Stable, 2 for Variable' — i.e. the mode being swapped FROM. BorrowLogic.executeSwapBorrowRateMode burns the named-mode debt and mints the OTHER mode, so SwapRateModeAction.new_mode (the mode AFTER the swap) is the COMPLEMENT of the arg: arg 1 (STABLE) -> new_mode variable; arg 2 (VARIABLE) -> new_mode stable. Mainnet Pool v3.4+ no longer exposes this selector, so chain 1 is intentionally absent from this manifest and enforced by surface/aave/pool-mainnet.

CoW Protocol native-ETH order placement. CoWSwapEthFlow.createOrder(EthFlowOrder.Data order) payable, selector 0x322bba21. This is the ON-CHAIN path users take to sell native ETH on CoW (an EOA cannot EIP-712-presign a WETH order without first wrapping, so ethflow wraps msg.value to WETH and places the order on-chain). Covers BOTH active mainnet ethflow contracts: 0xba3cb449bd2b4adddbc894d8697f5170800eadec (current, ~99% of ethflow) + 0x40a50cf069e992aa4536211b23f286ef88752187 (v1, minor but still active). EthFlowOrder.Data has NO sellToken field — the sell token is ALWAYS the wrapped native token (WETH 0xc02aaa39b223fe8d0a0e5c4f27ead9083c756cc2 on mainnet), so sell is baked. msg.value = order.sellAmount + order.feeAmount (the native ETH the user spends); sell_amount mirrors the off-chain Order mapping (= order.sellAmount, fee dropped). -> amm sign_intent_order with OnchainTx meta.nature (same economic intent as the off-chain Order — place a CoW limit order selling X for min Y to recipient, expiring at validTo — but established on-chain rather than by signature; meta.nature distinguishes it). venue=cow_swap, settlement=GPv2Settlement 0x9008d19f58aabd9ed0d60971565aa8510560ab41 (where the wrapped order settles). 1st-party: github.com/cowprotocol/ethflowcontract src/CoWSwapEthFlow.sol (createOrder) + src/libraries/EthFlowOrder.sol (Data struct).

CoW Protocol off-chain EIP-712 Order signature (the dominant CowSwap gasless-intent action). domain name='Gnosis Protocol' version='v2', verifying_contract=GPv2Settlement 0x9008d19f58aabd9ed0d60971565aa8510560ab41 (mainnet, verifyingContract=address(this)), primary_type=Order. Unmapped/plumbing legs (transfers, wraps, deferred adapters) are skipped; the lending legs carry the intent. recurse_arg=bundle. Call = (address to, bytes data, uint256 value, bool skipRevert, bytes32 callbackHash).

GeneralAdapter1 erc20Transfer plumbing leg (reached via Bundler3 multicall(Call[])). GA1 sends `amount` of `token` to `receiver` from its own balance (bundle funding / leftover sweep). Modeled as token/erc20_transfer so the per-bundle token movement (token + amount + recipient) is legible — all three are in the leg calldata.

GeneralAdapter1 erc20TransferFrom plumbing leg (reached via Bundler3 multicall(Call[])). GA1 pulls `amount` of `token` from the bundle initiator (the user, via the user's ERC20 approval) to `receiver` (typically GA1 itself, to fund a downstream deposit). This is the bundle's token-IN: the amount can EXCEED the deposit (over-pull), bounded only by the separately-gated approval — so surfacing it (token + amount + recipient, all in calldata) is the legibility win.

Permit2 invalidateNonces(token,spender,newNonce) invalidates ordered allowance nonces for a token/spender pair. This is modeled as a permission revocation for policy purposes; the exact nonce floor is not represented in RevokeScope today.

This revokes unordered nonce bitmap bits used by SignatureTransfer flows, including UniswapX PermitWitnessTransferFrom orders. It is modeled as Token::RevokeApproval with scope.kind=permit2_unordered_nonce so policy/UI can explain the nonce-word revoke directly instead of pretending wordPos is an order hash.

emit._note: unlockData = abi.encode(bytes actions, bytes[] params). The dispatcher pre-decodes it into (commands, inputs[]) — structurally identical to the Universal Router envelope — then runs the shared per-opcode dispatch. V4 actions are NOT masked (full byte 0x00-0x1b), so mask=0xff / allow_revert_bit=0x00. Settlement-only actions that pay PoolManager deltas (for example SETTLE/SETTLE_PAIR) remain skipped to avoid noisy Unknown legs on normal mint/increase flows. Recipient-bearing egress actions are explicit below: exact TAKE is modeled as token egress, while amountless or balance-dependent recipient actions such as TAKE_PAIR/SWEEP are surfaced as Unknown so payout redirection cannot vanish from policy evaluation. Swap codes (0x06-0x09) are UnsupportedAction inside modifyLiquidities (PositionManager table only) and are likewise skipped. V4 native currency address(0) is mapped to Core::TokenKey::Native via token_key_or_native_zero. pool_manager is injected per-chain by the route handler as $resolved.pool_manager (mainnet/Base/OP/ARB V4 PoolManager singletons).

0x01._note: DECREASE shares INCREASE's wire decoder (uint256 tokenId, uint256 liquidity, uint128, uint128, bytes); slots 2/3 are slippage LOWER bounds amount0Min/amount1Min (validateMinOut). liquidity is uint256 on the wire but bound into the U128 liquidity_burn (fits for every real position; > u128 would reject at deserialize, mirroring V3). pool_id NOT statically recoverable → 'unknown'.

0x02._note: MINT_POSITION is the only modifyLiquidities action fully self-describing from calldata: the PoolKey is encoded INLINE (head-flattened 5 fields: currency0, currency1, fee, tickSpacing, hooks) at the head of params[i], so the inputs_abi is a FLAT 12-field tuple (no nested offset). pool_id = keccak256(abi.encode(poolKey)) is computed in Rust by the dispatcher and injected as the synthetic $inputs.pool_id (the manifest can't hash). hooks/currency0/currency1 come straight from the inline PoolKey. owner is the recipient (address(1)=MSG_SENDER / address(2)=ADDRESS_THIS sentinels surface verbatim — sentinel→self mapping is a follow-up). amount0Max/amount1Max are slippage upper bounds. range.liquidity placeholder '0' (the position's minted liquidity is on-chain-assigned).

Mainnet only (ExclusiveDutchOrderReactor 0x6000da47…, 1차 SDK REACTOR_ADDRESS_MAPPING + Etherscan Exact Match, research §3.2/§3.3). EIP-712 type FLATTENS input → witness.inputToken/inputStartAmount/inputEndAmount. selector 0x00000001 is a sign-only placeholder (off-chain order is never an on-chain calldata call against this manifest; distinct per family to avoid by-callkey collision on the shared Permit2 address).

UniswapX PriorityOrder signed as a Permit2 permitWitnessTransferFrom witness — domain=Permit2, verifying_contract=canonical Permit2, primary_type=PermitWitnessTransferFrom, witness_type=PriorityOrder. reactor read from witness order.info.reactor. PriorityOrder KEEPS NESTED input/outputs (PriorityInput/PriorityOutput). MODELING APPROXIMATION: order_kind="limit" — priority orders fix amounts at sign time (the priority fee is the ordering mechanism, not a price-decay curve); IntentOrderKind has no Priority variant so "limit" is the least-wrong. Current ActionBody support is single-output only: PriorityOutput carries `amount` (no start/end) → sell_amount=input.amount, buy_min=sole output.amount; multi-output orders fail visible instead of truncating. cosignerData/cosignature are cosigner-added, EXCLUDED from the swapper witness. selector 0x00000004 is a sign-only placeholder (distinct per family).
